Welcome to Heathcote School
Our vision is to create a school that provides young people with a safe and happy learning environment that challenges and supports all learners to achieve their best outcomes through a creative, inspiring and enriched curriculum.
Upcoming Events
Open Morning Tours 2026
Families of Year 6, we invite you to come and tour our wonderful school.
We are once again running our popular Morning Tours this autumn. Tours are available on multiple dates between 14th September and 21st October, between 9am and 10am.
Book your place on Eventbrite using this link, or alternatively please scan the QR code below.
Open Evening 2026
Our Open Evening this year takes place on Wednesday 7th October from 5pm to 7.30pm.
Book your place on Eventbrite using this link or alternatively please scan the QR code below – we look forward to seeing you!
A Message From The Head
Our priority is school improvement and making sure that your child receives the best education both in the classroom and outside, ensuring nobody is left behind socially or academically and that we develop well-rounded individuals who are challenged and stretched whatever their starting point and who succeed in realising their ambitions.
Our Vision & Values
We aim to create a school that provides young people with a safe and happy learning environment that challenges and supports all learners to achieve their best outcomes through a creative, inspiring and enriched curriculum.
Our values of Encourage – Challenge – Succeed embody everything we do at Heathcote.
Encourage
We encourage our pupils to take pride in their learning and community – to work hard, be kind, display good manners and achieve to the best of their abilities. Pupils seek and embrace feedback and show understanding and mutual respect for each other and show excellent behaviour at all times.
Challenge
We challenge our pupils to push themselves, take responsibility for their learning, to be resilient to failure and to self-regulate their behaviour. All our staff and governors are determined that all pupils confidently strive for success and expect them to be present and punctual.
Succeed
We succeed when all pupils enjoy their learning and reach their academic potential in all areas; leaving Heathcote as thoughtful, caring and honest citizens fully prepared for the next stage of their life – whether that be in education, training or employment. We succeed by letting them do so in a comfortable and safe environment and culture where they take a proactive role and develop socially.

pageCache.text:
Wider Curriculum & Personal Development
At Heathcote’s Sixth Form, we recognise that education extends beyond the classroom, encompassing personal growth, well-being, and a holistic approach to development. Our commitment to nurturing well-rounded individuals is reflected in our Wider Curriculum & Personal Development initiatives
PIE Lessons
Engage in informative and supportive tutorial lessons that cover essential aspects of personal development. Our dedicated fortnightly sessions explore diverse topics such as career planning, university and apprenticeship guidance, mental well-being, and exam skills. These lessons aim to equip pupils with valuable life skills, fostering responsibility and awareness in a rapidly changing world.
Sports and Activities
Embrace a healthy and active lifestyle through our sports and activities programme. Heathcote provides access to a fully-equipped gym and organises weekly sports sessions to promote physical well-being. We believe that a healthy body contributes to a healthy mind, and our initiatives support pupils in maintaining balance and vitality in their lives.
Clubs and Projects
Participate in intellectually stimulating and socially enriching clubs and projects. Join the Debate Club to sharpen critical thinking and communication skills, explore the world of cinema with our Film Club, or make a positive impact through the Envision Project—a social action initiative that encourages pupils to contribute to meaningful causes and develop leadership abilities.
Academic Boosters
Receive personalised academic support to enhance your learning journey. Our booster programmes include one-to-one and small group tutoring sessions tailored to address specific academic needs. We also utilise the Up Learning online revision platform for STEM subjects, providing pupils with additional resources and interactive tools to reinforce their understanding. Whether you require assistance with complex concepts, exam preparation, or additional challenges, our experienced educators are here to guide you toward success.
At Heathcote Sixth Form, we are dedicated to fostering both academic achievement and personal development, preparing our pupils for a bright future.

Sports & Fixtures, Trips and Extra Curricular
Sports & Fixtures
Welcome to the sporting fixture area of the Heathcote School website! We are delighted to have you here as we recognise the vital role that sports play in fostering teamwork, discipline, and school community.
At Heathcote, we are committed to providing our pupils with numerous opportunities to engage in a variety of sports, promoting both physical health and personal growth.
A timetable of our upcoming fixtures, designed to keep you informed about the exciting sporting events we have planned, is sent home via Arbor each term and can also be found in the newsletter. We encourage both pupils and parents to stay updated and get involved, as your support and participation are key to the success of our sports programs. Thank you for being a part of the Heathcote sports community!
Enrichment - Trips and Visits
Heathcote School is steadfast in its commitment to enriching the educational experience through meaningful trips and visits. We believe that learning extends beyond the classroom, and these excursions serve as invaluable opportunities for pupils to connect theoretical knowledge with real-world applications.
Our commitment involves meticulously planning diverse and engaging trips that align with the curriculum, fostering experiential learning and broadening pupils’ perspectives. Whether exploring cultural landmarks, participating in scientific expeditions, or engaging in community service initiatives, these experiences contribute significantly to holistic development. At Heathcote School, we prioritize creating lasting memories and facilitating profound educational encounters through carefully curated trips and visits
For further information, please see our Educational Visits Policy available in the Policies section.
Extra Curricular Activities
Heathcote School takes great pride in offering a vibrant array of extra-curricular activities that go beyond the traditional academic setting. Our commitment to holistic education extends to a diverse range of clubs, sports, arts, and leadership programs, providing pupils with ample opportunities to explore their passions and talents.
Whether participating in sports teams, joining debate clubs, engaging in arts and cultural societies, or taking on leadership roles in pupil organisations, our extracurricular activities foster teamwork, creativity, and personal growth. These experiences not only complement academic achievements but also contribute to the development of well-rounded individuals. At Heathcote School, we encourage every pupil to discover and pursue their interests through our enriching extracurricular offerings.
For further information, please contact your child’s Year Lead.

Careers
CEIAG
Careers education, information, advice and guidance (CEIAG) is an essential part of the support we offer to pupils at Heathcote School & Science College. The CEIAG programme is designed to be progressive from Year 7 through to Year 13, and to support pupils in making choices at key moments in their chosen education and career pathway. A robust and stable careers programme helps avoid disengagement, puts school learning into a wider and relevant context, and raises aspirations.
At Heathcote School & Science College we aim to raise aspirations, challenge stereotypes and encourage pupils to consider a wide range of career pathways. Through their careers education and guidance, pupils are encouraged to make the most of their talents, and to pursue vocations that suit their needs and aspirations
For further information, please see our Careers Policy in the Policies section or contact Assistant Head Ms Sita Bashal. A guide from Waltham Forest can also be downloaded here.

Behaviour
Our Policy
At Heathcote School, we expect high standards of positive behaviour, both in school and out in the community. We believe that good behaviour underpins success and pupils can only reach their potential if their standard of behaviour is consistently high, and if learning is not disrupted by the negative behaviour of others.
With this in mind, our rewards serve to recognise and positively reinforce your child’s good behaviour and the sanctions serve as a consequence if our expectations are not met. As members of the Heathcote community, we believe that your child should understand that there are always consequences associated with good and bad behaviour.
We do not allow disruption to learning and do operate a lesson removal system where pupils are placed in an IEU for pupils that disrupt lessons on more than 2 occasions.
Please make sure you read our Behaviour Policy in the Policies section of the website.
Our Aims
Banned & Prohibited Items
To help us ensure a positive learning environment where your child and all other pupils’ primary focus is on their learning, there are a number of items that we do not permit pupils to bring into school for Health and Safety reasons and/ or because valuable teaching time can be lost when items are misplaced.
We request that parents/carers ensure that the following items are NOT brought into school under any circumstances. We therefore do not accept responsibility for any missing or stolen items that are listed below. Confiscated food and drink will be disposed of. The list is not exhaustive and may be subject to change by the Senior Leadership Team at any time. We operate searching, screening and the use of metal detector wands when required following government guidance.
Pupils will be sanctioned for bringing these items into school and likely to have them confiscated at the very least.
In addition, pupils are NOT ALLOWED to at any time:
Mobile phones, AIrpods.
Music devices and earphones
Expensive ICT devices
Electronic equipment including portable game consoles
Drugs, banned substances or drug paraphernalia
Fireworks
Lasers of any description

Jewellery (except small studs)
Sweets/ chocolate/ chewing gum

Wear excessive jewellery or body piercing

Ready, Respectful, Responsible
At Heathcote School our behaviour expectations are underpinned by our belief that our pupils should always be READY, RESPECTFUL and RESPONSIBLE.

Curriculum of Heathcote
At Heathcote’s Sixth Form, our curriculum is designed to provide a dynamic and comprehensive educational experience, ensuring that pupils are well-prepared for their future endeavours. We offer a diverse range of courses, allowing pupils to tailor their studies to align with their academic interests and career aspirations.
Our Extensive List of Courses
Our extensive list of courses spans both A’ Level and AAQ/BTEC Level 3 qualifications. Whether pupils have a passion for the sciences, humanities, arts, or vocational studies, our curriculum caters to a wide array of academic disciplines. Special Education Needs
SEN Provision
At Heathcote School, we will provide all pupils with access to a broad and balanced curriculum. We are focused on creating an inclusive environment, where provision is tailored to meet the needs and abilities of all our pupils, no matter how varied.
Our staff are committed to making sure all our pupils have the chance to thrive, providing the specific support needed to achieve their full potential. Our school environment is welcoming where all students feel supported, valued, safe and happy.
Pupils with EHCP in the mainstream school receive the interventions and support commensurate with the needs outlined on their EHCP. We also offer therapy sessions if required.
Please contact our SENDCO Rebecca Lewis if you have any further queries. She can be reached at rlewis@heathcote.waltham.sch.uk
Deaf Support Department (DSD)
The Deaf Support Department (DSD) currently caters for 18 students, aged 11-18. Each pupil has an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP) associated with an educationally significant hearing loss. All pupils in the DSD wear personal hearing instruments to support a total communication approach. These include hearing aids, (Bone Anchored Hearing Aids (BAHA) and cochlear implants.
Heathcote School utilises Soundfield systems in 50+ classes and DSD students have access to Radio Aids to support listening and learning.
The DSD has a moral responsibility to monitor the needs of deaf pupils who do not have an EHCP. This comes in the form of monitoring audiology equipment, highlighting deaf friendly strategies to teachers and offering advice to parents.

Careers Beyond Sixth Form
Nurturing Future Success
At Heathcote Sixth Form, our commitment to nurturing the future success of our pupils is evident through a range of initiatives designed to support their transition into higher education, apprenticeships, or employment. Personalised one-on-one careers guidance ensures that each pupil receives tailored advice, helping them explore diverse career paths and make informed decisions.
Our PIE focus lessons extends beyond the classroom, emphasising practical career development skills. Pupils engage in sessions that hone their abilities in creating quality CVs, mastering effective interview techniques, and cultivating the professional skills necessary for success in the workplace.
In Year 12, pupils gain hands-on experience through work placements, providing them with valuable insights into their chosen fields and enabling the application of theoretical knowledge in real-world settings. This exposure not only enhances their understanding of various professions but also helps them make informed decisions about their future career paths.
Heathcote Sixth Form values partnerships with leading companies, such as Zurich, which offers career mentorship to our pupils. These collaborations provide pupils with a unique opportunity to benefit from the experiences and insights of seasoned professionals, fostering a direct connection between classroom learning and real-world application.
As a result, Heathcote pupils are well-supported in their transition to higher education, apprenticeships, or employment. Many have successfully progressed to competitive Russell Group universities like Oxford and Cambridge, while others have secured apprenticeships with prominent companies such as TFL, Barratt, and Mace. Our holistic approach to preparing pupils for their future endeavours ensures they are well-equipped and confident as they step into the next chapter of their lives.

About Pupil Premium
At Heathcote School, our unwavering commitment to pupil premium pupils is at the heart of our educational philosophy. Recognizing the unique challenges that these pupils may face; we are dedicated to providing tailored support and resources to ensure their academic success and personal development. Through targeted interventions, personalised learning plans, and a nurturing environment, we strive to empower every pupil premium student, fostering an inclusive and equitable educational experience. Our aim is not only to bridge gaps but to inspire and cultivate the full potential of each individual, fostering a positive and enriching educational journey at Heathcote School.

Head of Music

Heathcote School and Science College is an inclusive community school with key values to Encourage, Challenge and Succeed. The values are integral in everything we do to support and nurture pupils to achieve the best possible outcomes in a safe and happy learning environment. Feedback from our recent Ofsted report (February 2024) confirmed Staff greatly enjoy working at the school. They hugely value the support they receive for their workload and well-being.
We are seeking to appoint an innovative, solution focused and inspirational Department Lead to grow and develop the Music department and to teach the full ability range, including GCSE. You will play a key role in the progressive development of Music ensuring outstanding participation and progress for pupils.
The school puts well-being and development at the heart of its work, and we have very talented staff who are encouraged to grow and develop collaboratively, within school and with local schools, to be the best they can be. We are working to raise standards in a ‘high challenge, low threat’ way and enable robust systems which ensure consistency in all areas and encourage growth and development for all. The school has excellent resources and an impressive, spacious site on the edge of Epping Forest including a staff car park and surrounding roads that do not require a parking permit. We are also a 15-minute walk from Chingford Station which has great links into the City.

Assessments & Reporting
About
Heathcote School & Science College recognises that pupils and parents / carers are keen to know how they are progressing, however, we are also aware that assessment can impact both teacher and pupil wellbeing. Heathcote takes a balanced approach to assessment which means that we have accurate information to help pupils progress with regard for pupils and teacher workload.
Teachers regularly assess pupils at Heathcote School. We use a variety of methods of assessment including monitoring pupil progress in lessons, coursework assignments, in-class tests and more traditional formal exams.
Challenge Weeks
A distinctive feature of assessment at Heathcote is Challenge Weeks. Challenge Weeks are held twice a year for all year groups. This is an opportunity for pupils to be assessed in all their subjects. Our Challenge Week cycle has a number of benefits for pupils:
Reporting
We report to parents three times a year. Our reports include information about your child’s academic progress, their effort and their homework. We also provide opportunities for you to discuss your child’s progress with their teachers once a year at a parents’ evening. If you have question or concerns about your child’s progress during the year, please do not hesitate to contact the subject teacher.
